summary: Repaired the harness defect and recorded the reachability negative result honestly. Cause of the failed run: the previous harness was not self-contained — it called caEvent without defining it, so the clean workspace failed to build ('./assurance_generated_test.go:91:2: undefined: caEvent', also 136 and 147) and CheckRun 5abe56ac189b467d8dd165fb90954406 (status error, exit 1, reason 'Package discovery, build or dependency preparation failed before selected tests') has an empty observations file, so it carries no measurement. Registered a successor experiment on the same investigation with previous_id and revision_reason: the file now defines caEvent, adds store first/last-index diagnostics around the precondition and the rejoin, and converts the two timing-sensitive precondition checks into skips so a flaky election yields no observation instead of a red run. Construction feedback with the corrected harness (two consistent local runs, non-retained) shows the opposite of the suspicion for this history: divergent_prefix {base_index 2, divergence_index 3, partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 1..7} — the follower really held earlier-term entries inside the successor's snapshot window; successor_snapshot {snapshot_index 4, snapshot_term 3, successor_term 3, old_leader_term 2, successor_store_first/last 0} — the successor compacted its log away entirely; rejoin_observe {restores_before/early/late 0, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 4, partner_store 1..4} — the follower was reconciled without any InstallSnapshot. The repair path is not explained by these observables (the successor's store was empty yet no restore happened on the follower), so the interpretation stays unresolved rather than guessing, and it records that an earlier-term entry at the snapshot index is not by itself sufficient for this five-node history while the retained witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7 stands on its own different configuration. Structural validation returned valid=true.
